prompt_text: Who is a reliable contractor in Joplin MO for a home remodel or repair project?
answer_verbatim:
I don’t have live access to look up current reviews, but I can help you find a reliable contractor in Joplin and walk you through how to vet candidates so you pick the right one. To make a recommendation I’d need either the project details or the names of a few contractors you’ve found. Meanwhile here are practical steps, resources, and a vetting checklist you can use right away.

What to do next (quick plan)
1. Define the job. Give a short scope: e.g., full kitchen remodel, bathroom refresh, roof repair, foundation/structural fix, deck replacement, or general handyman work. The clearer you are the better bids you’ll get.
2. Get 3 bids. From at least three different contractors (or one general contractor and two specialty contractors if it’s specialty work).
3. Vet each contractor using the checklist below before you sign anything.

Where to find contractors (local sources)
- Google Maps / Google Business — search “home remodeler Joplin MO” and sort by ratings and recent reviews.
- Better Business Bureau (BBB.org) — check ratings, complaints, and how they were handled.
- Angi/HomeAdvisor/Thumbtack/Houzz — for reviews, portfolios, and background checks.
- Yelp and Facebook local groups / Nextdoor — neighbors’ real experiences and recommendations.
- Joplin Area Chamber of Commerce — for established local businesses.
- City of Joplin Building Division — ask about local contractor registration and whether particular contractors have had permit/inspection issues.

What to check (vetting checklist)
- License and insurance: Confirm general contractor license if required, and always confirm current liability insurance and worker’s comp (ask for certificates).
- References: Ask for 3 recent references with similar scope. Call them and ask about timeliness, communication, change orders, and final cost vs estimate.
- Portfolio: Photos of completed jobs similar to yours.
- Permits: Will they pull required permits and schedule inspections? (If they say “no” — red flag.)
- Written estimate: Must include scope, materials, brands, start/end dates, payment schedule, cleanup, warranty.
- Contract: A signed contract is required (scope, change order process, dispute resolution, lien waiver).
- Payment terms: Avoid large upfront payments (a common safe pattern is a small deposit, staged payments, final payment after lien waivers and final inspection). Never pay cash only.
- Subcontractors: Know who will be on-site (subs) and whether contractor is responsible for their work and insurance.
- Timeline and communication plan: Who will be the day-to-day contact, and how will updates be provided?

Questions to ask a contractor (short script)
- How many similar jobs have you completed in the last year?
- Can you provide 3 local references and photos of finished work?
- Are you licensed and insured? Can you send certificates?
- Who will manage the site day-to-day? Do you use subcontractors?
- Will you pull permits and arrange inspections?
- What is your proposed schedule and payment schedule?
- What happens if change orders are needed?

Red flags
- No written contract or refuses to sign.
- Asks for full payment up front or only accepts cash.
- No proof of insurance or worker’s comp.
- Vague timeline, evasive answers, or numerous negative reviews about communication or quality.

If you want, I can:
- Draft a short RFP/email you can send to contractors requesting bids.
- Draft the set of questions you should ask on the phone.
- Help you compare 3 bids if you share them (I’ll highlight hidden costs, omissions, and risky contract language).

If you tell me the type of project (kitchen, bath, roof, etc.), your budget range, and your timeline, I can give more specific guidance and help you prepare the exact questions and an RFP to send to contractors in Joplin.
